text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Srbian President Slobodan Milosevic answers letter addressed to him by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in which he says peace, democracy and economic development are basic goals of Yugoslavia's policy.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini who said elections cannot be repeated, sanctions will not be introduced and called for opening of a dialogue with the opposition.
- Opposition leader Vuk Draskovic said after talks with Lamberto Dini the opposition first asks for recognition of November election results before entering dialogue.
- It is difficult that problems of succession of the former Yugoslavia will be resovled at the level of expert groups, says Yugoslav federal government commision.
- Electricity price rises by an average of 60 percent from December 5, in relation to summer electricity prices.
- The Serbian government proposes formation of special coordination team for private enterprise to more actively include entrepreneurs in all phases of drafting laws.
- Yugoslavia must considerably increase its exports next year despite difficulties, says President of the Yugosalv Chamber of Commerce Mihajlo Milojevic.
- Basket of basic food and drink products for a four-member family stood at 1,451 dinars in November which is down 1.7 percent on the previous month, according to official statistics.
NASA BORBA
- Montenegrin authorities called on Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to resolve the political crisis as soon as possible.
- Over 200 Novi Sad students setting off on foot to Belgrade (75kms away) to join their Belgrade collegues in protest over annullment of election results.
- Demonstrations in Belgrade and other Serbian cities continue over annullment of election results.
- Independent association of Serbian journalists gathering signatures for petition demanding free press. The Association plans to submit the petition to Serbian parliament.
POLITKA EKSPRES
- Serbian Chamber of Commerce discusses bank insolvency, on the average at least 45 banks fall into the red every day.
- The drivers' union of the city transport company (GSP) fails to organise strike Tuesday. Director of GSP Mihajlo Glavicic submits resignation without citing reasons.
BORBA
- Schools and faculties in Serbia work normally and are open to those students who attend, said Serbian Education Minister Dragoslav Mladenovic.
